chunks: ʿAbdullāh ibn Maymūn narrated from Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said:
Two rakʿahs performed by a married person are better than seventy rakʿahs performed by an unmarried person.
ai.seo_question: Why are two rakʿahs of a married person considered better than seventy rakʿahs of an unmarried person?
ai.summary: This hadith states the great merit of the married person, showing that marriage enhances and dignifies one's acts of worship. It highlights the spiritual virtue associated with marriage and the elevated worth of salat performed within that state.
